blocks.text: , Tuesday: Choroní and the Coastal Beaches

provenance.rationale: Uses the Word’s Day 2 location and beach context, with the weekday and wording of the RU title.

blocks.text:
Free time to relax. Optional boat trips to nearby beaches are available.

El Arao is a small beach with clear water where the river meets the sea and forms a lagoon. Uricao is considered one of the most beautiful and least developed beaches on this coast. Cuyagua is popular with surfers.

Chuao is one of the most popular beaches in Aragua State. Nearby is the village of El Chuao, founded in 1660. You can take a walk and visit an estate that grows high-quality Criollo cacao. More than 20 tonnes of cacao are produced there each year.

El Sepé has palm trees, clear water and white sand. Food and drinks are available, and you can walk to the river. Tuja is a sheltered bay with turquoise water, rivers and waterfalls. Paddleboarding, snorkelling, diving and fishing are available.

Ciénaga de Ocumare is a bay with a natural pool and clear water. You can swim, kayak through the mangroves, snorkel or take a mud bath. Fresh fish and seafood are cooked on the beach. Look for seabirds and sea stars in the bay. With luck, you may also see a green turtle.

Meals: breakfast and dinner.
